resources.string: Answer separately, then see where you already agree
Each of you answers on your own. Nobody sees a half being written, and neither of you can edit the other\'s. Where you both tick the other\'s answer, the question counts as agreed.
This is not the Ministry of Justice form. It covers the same areas the law and that form name, in our own words.
The point of a parenting plan is that both of you answer and then compare. Connect with your co-parent to start one.
Write it as you would say it to a mediator
If either of you edits an answer, the agreement lapses and you tick again.
Talking to each other and settling disagreements
Where will the child live, and which address will be registered as their home?
How will you decide if one of you wants to move, and how much notice will you give?
How will you divide weekdays, weekends and school holidays between you?
Where and when will handovers happen, and who takes the child there?
How will you divide the school holidays each year?
How will birthdays, Christmas and other family occasions be spent?
Which school or nursery will the child attend, and who deals with the school?
Which activities will the child do, and who arranges and pays for them?
Which doctors will the child be registered with, and how will you keep each other informed?
How will a decision about treatment that can wait be taken?
What maintenance will be paid, by whom, and on what day of the month?
How will one-off costs — glasses, a school trip, a laptop — be shared?
How will you pass on information about the child, and how quickly do you expect a reply?
What will you do when you cannot agree?
